h: Little Things That Make the Big Wheel Better
p: A few numbers to impress whoever you're sharing a capsule with. The wheel stands around 135 metres tall and carries 32 capsules, one for each of London's boroughs. There's no number 13, though, so the capsules run up to 33 to dodge the unlucky one. Each pod fits a couple of dozen people, which means you'll usually be sharing with strangers unless you've booked a private one for a big occasion.

Where you stand matters. Head to the end of the capsule facing the direction of travel early on and you'll get the best of Westminster as you climb, then shuffle round for the views east towards the City as you come over the top. There's a bench in the middle for anyone who'd rather sit and soak it in. The glass can pick up reflections, so pressing your phone close to it gives cleaner photos.

Timing-wise, the ride itself is short, but allow extra for security checks and getting to your boarding slot, especially in school holidays. Jubilee Gardens right next door is a handy patch of grass for a sit-down with a snack before or after, and the London Eye Pier alongside is where river cruises set off, so it's easy to turn sky-high views into a gentle trip along the Thames too. Mornings and weekdays outside the holidays tend to feel calmer than a summer Saturday afternoon.
